subs.label: Crime
subs.axis: Axis: by the criminal world and engine the story is built on — organised crime and its named national cycles first, then street-crime cycles, the heist and the swindle, the law's agents, prison and courts, real and social crime; noir as a mode and crime played for laughs last

leaves.label: Gangster Film
leaves.defn: A film whose protagonist is a member or boss of a criminal organisation and whose story is the gang's rise, wars and fall (Little Caesar, Once Upon a Time in America, Gomorrah, Vada Chennai). Hindi-language underworld films go to A2-2 Mumbai Noir, Japanese ones to A2-3; a film that follows the police against the mob goes to A2-15/A2-16.
leaves.aliases: mob film; mafia film; underworld film
leaves.see: A2-2 Mumbai Noir; A2-3 Yakuza Film; A2-25 Neo-Noir
leaves.axis: by the criminal tradition: the classical American cycle and the mafia saga first, then crime-boss biography and the national gangster traditions

leaves.label: Mumbai Noir
leaves.defn: A Hindi-language film of the Bombay underworld (or its Shakespearean transpositions to the gangland of the Hindi heartland), shot in a realist, violent register (Satya, Maqbool, Omkara). South Indian gangster sagas stay in A2-1.
leaves.see: A2-1 Gangster Film

leaves.label: Yakuza Film
leaves.defn: A film about the Japanese yakuza, from the ninkyo chivalry films through Fukasaku's jitsuroku and Kitano's deadpan cycle (Battles Without Honor and Humanity, Sonatine, Outrage).
leaves.aliases: yakuza eiga; ninkyo eiga; jitsuroku eiga
leaves.see: A2-1 Gangster Film; A2-24 Film Noir

leaves.label: Poliziottesco
leaves.defn: An Italian crime-action film of the 1970s cycle of violent cops, mobsters and kidnappers (Caliber 9, Rabid Dogs).
leaves.see: A2-16 Police Film

leaves.label: Hitman Film
leaves.defn: A film whose protagonist is a professional killer and whose drama is the contract, its code and its cost (The Mechanic, Ghost Dog, The American, The Killer). Stylised existential killers of the Melville line sit in A2-25 Neo-Noir.
leaves.see: A2-25 Neo-Noir; A3-10 Revenge Thriller

leaves.label: Drug Film
leaves.defn: A crime film whose engine is the illegal drug trade or drug addiction: cartels and mules, the dealer's world, the junkie's crimes (Traffic, Maria Full of Grace, Pusher, Drugstore Cowboy).
leaves.see: A2-8 Hood Film; A2-16 Police Film
leaves.axis: by the place in the trade: the cartel and the trafficking route first, then the dealer's street world, then the addict

leaves.label: Blaxploitation
leaves.defn: A 1970s American exploitation film made for Black urban audiences, with Black heroes against the Man, pimps and pushers (Shaft, Super Fly, Coffy), including its horror and Afrofuturist offshoots.
leaves.see: A2-8 Hood Film

leaves.label: Hood Film
leaves.defn: An African-American (or Caribbean, Latino and Black British) film of street life, gangs and drugs in the inner-city neighbourhood (Boyz n the Hood, Menace II Society, Kidulthood).
leaves.see: A2-7 Blaxploitation; A2-22 Social Problem Film

leaves.label: Cine Quinqui
leaves.defn: A Spanish film of the late-1970s/80s cycle about juvenile delinquents of the urban periphery, often cast with real delinquents (Deprisa, Deprisa).
leaves.see: A2-22 Social Problem Film

leaves.label: Pinky Violence
leaves.defn: A 1970s Toei exploitation film of female gangs and avenging women prisoners (Female Prisoner #701: Scorpion).
leaves.see: A2-19 Prison Film; A3-10 Revenge Thriller

leaves.label: Heist Film
leaves.defn: A film built around planning and executing a robbery, told from the thieves' side (Rififi, Ocean's Eleven, Heat, Reservoir Dogs). A swindle with no break-in goes to A2-12; a standoff with hostages to A3-12.
leaves.see: A2-12 Con-Artist Film; A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller
leaves.axis: by the heist's engine: the meticulous caper and the ensemble crew first, then the job that goes wrong, the professional thief, action spectacle; comic heists last

leaves.label: Con-Artist Film
leaves.defn: A film whose engine is a confidence trick: grifters, swindlers and the marks they play, often with a twist that cons the viewer (Nine Queens, House of Games, The Grifters, Focus).
leaves.aliases: con film; grifter film; swindle film
leaves.see: A2-11 Heist Film; A2-13 White-Collar Crime Film

leaves.label: White-Collar Crime Film
leaves.defn: A film about crime committed by the respectable in suits: fraud, embezzlement, financial and corporate crime (Wall Street, Boiler Room, Arbitrage, Lord of War).
leaves.see: A2-12 Con-Artist Film; A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller

leaves.label: Gambling Film
leaves.defn: A crime film whose world is the gambling table and the debt it creates (Rounders, Croupier, Uncut Gems, Hard Eight).
leaves.see: A2-12 Con-Artist Film

leaves.label: Police Procedural
leaves.defn: A film that follows police or federal investigators working a case step by step, its drama in the method of the inquiry (Stray Dog, The Night of the 12th, In the Heat of the Night, Mississippi Burning). A hunt for a serial killer goes to A3-6; a film about the cop's own conduct goes to A2-16.
leaves.see: A2-16 Police Film; A3-6 Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.axis: by the investigating force: city homicide squads first, then the rural lawman, the federal agent

leaves.label: Police Film
leaves.defn: A film whose subject is the police officer rather than the case: the rule-breaking maverick, the corrupt cop, the undercover cop, the beat or tactical unit (Dirty Harry, Training Day, Infernal Affairs, Elite Squad).
leaves.see: A2-15 Police Procedural; A2-1 Gangster Film
leaves.axis: by the cop's relation to the law: the maverick first, then corruption, life undercover, the street and tactical unit

leaves.label: Nordic Noir
leaves.defn: A Scandinavian crime film in the bleak, procedural, socially critical Nordic-noir manner (The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, Department Q, Insomnia 1997).
leaves.see: A2-15 Police Procedural

leaves.label: Private-Eye Film
leaves.defn: A film whose investigator is a private detective outside the noir canon: modern and comic private eyes and gentleman sleuths (Harper, Gone Baby Gone, Detective Byomkesh Bakshy!, Veronica Mars). Classic hardboiled eyes go to A2-24 and A2-25; closed-circle puzzles to A3-1.
leaves.see: A2-24 Film Noir; A3-1 Whodunit

leaves.label: Prison Film
leaves.defn: A film set inside a prison whose drama is incarceration itself: escape, survival among inmates, guard and riot (The Shawshank Redemption, Escape from Alcatraz, A Prophet, A Man Escaped).
leaves.see: A2-10 Pinky Violence; A2-20 Legal Drama
leaves.axis: by what the prisoner wants: out first, then survival inside, then the action brawl; political and wartime prisons last

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A film whose drama runs through the legal process: trial, appeal, jury and death row (The Third Murder, The Life of David Gale, The Juror).
leaves.see: A2-19 Prison Film; A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller

leaves.label: True-Crime Film
leaves.defn: A dramatisation of a real crime case, centred on the criminal, the victim or the case itself rather than on a fictional investigation (In Cold Blood, 10 Rillington Place, Snowtown, Killers of the Flower Moon).
leaves.see: A3-6 Serial-Killer Thriller; A11 Biographical Film
leaves.axis: by whose story is told: the killer first, then the abducted victim, the notorious case, the swindle

leaves.label: Social Problem Film
leaves.defn: A crime film that presents crime as the product of a social condition, youth, gangs, slum, poverty or vice, rather than as a genre puzzle (The Young and the Damned, City of God, Pickpocket, A Touch of Sin).
leaves.aliases: social realist crime film; juvenile-delinquency film
leaves.see: A2-8 Hood Film; A2-9 Cine Quinqui; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the social condition: youth first, then the gang, the slum, poverty and desperation; vice exposés last

leaves.label: Lovers-on-the-Run Film
leaves.defn: A film of a criminal couple in flight from the law, the outlaw road movie of Bonnie and Clyde (You Only Live Once, Breathless 1983, True Romance, Ain't Them Bodies Saints).
leaves.see: A2-24 Film Noir; A2-25 Neo-Noir

leaves.label: Film Noir
leaves.defn: A crime film of the classical noir period (c.1940–1960), and its pre-war precursors and contemporaries abroad, with fatalistic, shadowed visual style and doomed protagonists (Double Indemnity, Out of the Past, The Asphalt Jungle, Touchez pas au grisbi). Post-classical noir goes to A2-25.
leaves.see: A2-25 Neo-Noir; A2-23 Lovers-on-the-Run Film
leaves.axis: by the noir plot engine: the femme fatale and the private eye first, then gang and heist noir, the wrong man, the police; the national noirs abroad last

leaves.label: Neo-Noir
leaves.defn: A post-classical crime film that revives noir's fatalism, moral ambiguity and stylisation (Chinatown, Blood Simple, Le Samouraï, Drive). Classical-period noir goes to A2-24.
leaves.see: A2-24 Film Noir; A2-5 Hitman Film
leaves.axis: by the noir engine: the private eye and the femme fatale first, then country noir, the professional criminal, the payback, the dream; the national new noirs and pastiche last

leaves.label: Crime Comedy
leaves.defn: A crime film played for laughs: bungling crooks and mob farce (The Pope of Greenwich Village, Amateur, Caught Stealing). Comic heists stay in A2-11; most crime comedies are in A12 Comedy.
leaves.see: A2-11 Heist Film; A12 Comedy

subs.label: Thriller & Mystery
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of suspense — the puzzle to be solved first, then the predator, the threatened mind and home, the abduction and the trap, the hunt and the chase; the state and its secrets last

leaves.label: Whodunit
leaves.defn: A mystery whose engine is the fair-play puzzle of which suspect committed the murder, solved by a detective (Murder on the Orient Express, Gosford Park, Knives Out). Inquiries by police squads go to A2-15.
leaves.see: A3-2 Inverted Detective Story; A2-18 Private-Eye Film
leaves.axis: by the shape of the puzzle: the great detective first, then the closed circle, the comic sleuths, the modern ensemble; twist-puzzle thrillers last

leaves.label: Inverted Detective Story
leaves.defn: A crime story that shows the murder and the murderer first, its suspense in the cover-up and the investigator closing in (Drishyam, Match Point, A Hard Day, Dial M for Murder).
leaves.see: A3-1 Whodunit

leaves.label: Mystery Film
leaves.defn: A mystery whose enigma is not a murder puzzle but a disappearance, a buried past or a riddle, pursued by an ordinary person (Bunny Lake Is Missing, A Simple Favor, The Da Vinci Code, Blow-Up).
leaves.see: A3-1 Whodunit; A3-7 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by the enigma: the disappearance first, then the buried past, the esoteric riddle; the unresolved art-film enigma last

leaves.label: Krimi
leaves.defn: A West German Edgar Wallace (or Bryan Edgar Wallace) crime-mystery film of the 1959–1972 Rialto cycle (Face of the Frog).
leaves.see: A3-5 Giallo; A3-1 Whodunit

leaves.label: Giallo
leaves.defn: An Italian murder-mystery thriller of the 1960s–80s cycle: black-gloved killer, stylised set-piece murders, amateur sleuth (Blood and Black Lace, The Bird with the Crystal Plumage, Deep Red).
leaves.see: A3-6 Serial-Killer Thriller; A4 Horror

leaves.label: Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is a serial or spree killer, followed by the hunter, the killer himself or the survivor (The Silence of the Lambs, Zodiac, The Chaser). Dramatised portraits of real killers go to A2-21.
leaves.see: A2-15 Police Procedural; A2-21 True-Crime Film; A3-5 Giallo
leaves.axis: by whose eyes: the manhunt first, then the killer's own, then the threatened witness or survivor

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose threat comes from the mind: a protagonist's unstable perception, a double, lost memory, obsession or a mind game played on them (Vertigo, Memento, Black Swan, Shutter Island). Threats from spouse, family or lodger go to A3-8.
leaves.see: A3-8 Domestic Thriller; A3-3 Mystery Film
leaves.axis: by the source of the threat: the unreliable mind first, then the double, lost identity, obsession, the impostor; the mind game played by another last

leaves.label: Domestic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose danger lives in the home and its intimacies: the murderous spouse, the intruder who moves in, the stalker, the poisoned family (Gaslight, Sleeping with the Enemy, The Hand That Rocks the Cradle, Single White Female). Desire-driven danger goes to A3-9..
leaves.aliases: domestic noir; '...from hell' thriller; female Gothic
leaves.see: A3-7 Psychological Thriller; A3-9 Erotic Thriller; A3-13 Home-Invasion Thriller
leaves.axis: by who threatens: the spouse first, then the intruder who moves in, the stalker, the family itself

leaves.label: Erotic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which sexual desire is the engine of danger and crime (Body Heat, Fatal Attraction, Basic Instinct, The Handmaiden).
leaves.see: A3-8 Domestic Thriller; A2-25 Neo-Noir; A15 Erotic Film
leaves.axis: by the shape of the danger: the femme fatale first, then the obsessive affair, voyeurism, the art-house variant; sexual power games last

leaves.label: Revenge Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is the protagonist's vengeance for a wrong (Death Wish, Oldboy, I Spit on Your Grave, Blue Ruin).
leaves.see: A2-5 Hitman Film; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the shape of the vengeance: the Korean revenge cycle first, then the vigilante, rape and revenge, the personal vendetta; the revenge action spree last

leaves.label: Kidnapping Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is an abduction: the ransom demand, the frantic search, or the captive's ordeal (High and Low, Ransom, Prisoners, Misery).
leaves.see: A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller; A2-21 True-Crime Film
leaves.axis: by the kidnapper's aim: ransom first, then abduction and the search, then captivity

leaves.label: Hostage & Siege Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller of a standoff: hostages taken, a building besieged, a plane or train hijacked (The Negotiator, Toy Soldiers, Captain Phillips, The Taking of Pelham One Two Three).
leaves.see: A2-11 Heist Film; A3-13 Home-Invasion Thriller
leaves.axis: by the place held: the standoff first, then the siege, then the hijacked vehicle

leaves.label: Home-Invasion Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which intruders break into a home and hold or hunt its occupants (Panic Room, Cold Creek Manor, Borgman).
leaves.see: A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller; A4 Horror

leaves.label: Survival Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller of staying alive against nature, a pursuer or a trap (Deliverance, Duel, Buried, Alive).
leaves.see: A3-15 Death Game Film; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by the hostile space: wilderness first, then the road and its pursuers, the water, the confined trap; escape from civil unrest last

leaves.label: Death Game Film
leaves.defn: A film in which people are forced into a lethal game or contest with rules (Battle Royale, The Hunger Games, Cube, Escape Room), including the human hunt of The Most Dangerous Game.
leaves.see: A3-14 Survival Thriller; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Real-Time Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose suspense depends on unfolding in (near) real time in a confined frame, a phone line, a screen or a race against the clock (Phone Booth, The Guilty, Run Lola Run, Profile).
leaves.see: A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller

leaves.label: Wrong-Man Thriller
leaves.defn: A Hitchcockian thriller of an innocent accused or mistaken for someone else, who must flee and prove his innocence (The 39 Steps, North by Northwest, The Fugitive, Tell No One).
leaves.see: A3-21 Spy Film; A2-24 Film Noir

leaves.label: Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which the protagonist uncovers a hidden plot by the powerful, the state, corporations or secret societies (The Parallax View, All the President's Men, The Insider, Enemy of the State).
leaves.see: A3-19 Political Thriller; A3-21 Spy Film
leaves.axis: by who conspires: the shadowy cabal of the paranoid thriller first, then corporations, then the press investigation, then the state cover-up

leaves.label: Political Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose stakes are political power itself: assassination, terrorism, military crisis, dictatorship, intrigue (Z, The Day of the Jackal, The Lives of Others, Conclave).
leaves.see: A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller; A3-21 Spy Film
leaves.axis: by the political threat: assassination first, then terror, military and nuclear crisis, dictatorship; intrigue for office last

leaves.label: Techno-Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is a technology: hacking, surveillance, AI, computer crime (The Net, Blackhat, Eagle Eye, Who Am I).
leaves.see: A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Spy Film
leaves.defn: A film about espionage: agents, moles and covert operations for a state (Notorious, The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, Dr. No, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy).
leaves.see: A3-22 Spy Comedy; A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.axis: by the spy's war: the World Wars first, then the Cold War, the spy-action franchise, the covert operation, today's intelligence world; the inter-Korean spy film last

leaves.label: Spy Comedy
leaves.defn: A spy film played for laughs or as a parody of the genre (The Tall Blond Man with One Black Shoe, True Lies, Spy, Kingsman).
leaves.see: A3-21 Spy Film; A12 Comedy
